transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith, nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well... I guess what brings me in is I just don't have the push I used to have. I used to do choir, and my quilting, and go visiting folks. But lately, most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. I know people are expecting me to be there, but I just sit instead.
About how long have you been feeling this way and pulling back from choir, quilting, and visiting people—days, weeks, or longer?
Well, it's been longer than days or weeks. I'd say this has been building up for a while now... probably since I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago.
During this time, have you also been feeling sad, down, or hopeless nearly every day, or is it mainly that you lack motivation without feeling sad?

No, I don't think I feel sad, really. I don't sit around crying or feeling bad about things. It's... it's more like what you said at the end there. I just don't have the get-up-and-go anymore. The motivation is just gone, but I wouldn't call it feeling down or hopeless.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory or ability to concentrate, or trouble keeping track of things you used to handle easily?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My memory seems fine, and I can still keep track of things just like I always did. It's not that I can't concentrate on things... I just don't have the desire to start them. My mind still works fine, it's just the drive that's gone.
Have you noticed any tremor, stiffness, or slowness in your movements—like your hands shaking or feeling stiff when you walk?

No, I haven't had any of that. My hands don't shake at all. And I guess... well, I don't feel stiff or slow when I walk, either. My body moves just fine when I actually get up to do something, I just don't have the drive to do it much. But no, no shaking or stiffness.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold, gaining weight, having dry skin or hair, or feeling more tired than usual lately?

No, I haven't noticed any of that. I'm not unusually cold, and my weight hasn't changed. My skin and hair are just the same as always. I mean, I guess I'm a little tired sometimes, but not more than usual. It's really just the motivation that's the issue, not feeling tired or cold or anything like that.
When you do manage to do something you used to enjoy, like singing in choir or quilting, do you still get pleasure or satisfaction from it, or does it feel flat and unrewarding now?

Well, it just feels kind of flat, I guess. I just don't have the push I used to have for choir, or the quilting, or even visiting folks. Most days I just sit at home with the TV on low... even though I know people are expecting me to show up. It just doesn't bring me that same feeling anymore, so I mostly just stay home.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite, or found yourself feeling guilty or worthless, since this started?

No, I haven't noticed any of that. I sleep fine, mostly. And I'm still eating my regular meals, so my appetite hasn't changed. I don't feel guilty or worthless, either... I just don't have the energy to do the things I used to. But no, my sleeping and eating are just fine, and I don't feel bad about myself.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions—like a stroke, heart problems, diabetes, or any other neurological issue—around the time this lack of motivation started?

No, I haven't had any of those things. No strokes or heart problems... no diabetes, either. My doctor hasn't told me I have any new medical issues or anything like that. Physically, I'm doing okay, really. It's just... well, just what I was saying before about not having the drive to do much. But no, no new medical problems.
Have people close to you noticed any changes in your personality—like becoming more irritable, impulsive, or acting in ways that seem out of character—since this started?

Well, I wouldn't say I've been irritable or impulsive, really. But I guess folks have noticed me acting a bit strange lately, doing things that aren't quite like me. 

Like when I go down to the senior center... sometimes I'll just get up and start moving the chairs around, putting them into school-type rows. Or I'll sit there and fold the exact same quilt square over and over again. The other ladies there will ask me to stop, but I just keep doing it. And the thing is, afterward, I can't rightly explain to them what I was doing or why I did it. So I suppose that's definitely a bit out of character for me.
Have you or others noticed you repeating other actions or sticking to the same routines over and over, like checking things repeatedly or insisting on doing tasks in a very specific order?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, besides what I just told you about moving the chairs and the quilt squares... I don't do things like checking the locks over and over, or needing to do my chores in an exact order. 

My days are pretty simple, really. I don't have any strict routines that I get stuck on or anything. So, no, I wouldn't say I do any of that kind of repeating.

Have you or others noticed you saying or doing things in public that seem socially inappropriate or insensitive—things you wouldn't have done before—like making blunt comments or not seeming to notice how others react to you?

No, I don't think so. I haven't been making rude comments or anything like that. I mean, I mostly just keep to myself. I haven't noticed people getting upset with things I say, and no one's told me I'm being insensitive. So, no, I wouldn't say I've been doing anything like that.
Have you or your family noticed any trouble managing things like your finances, medications, or planning tasks that you used to handle easily on your own?

No, I manage all that just fine. I still pay my own bills, and I take my pills when I'm supposed to. My daughter comes by sometimes to check in, but she hasn't had to take over my checkbook or anything. I handle my own business same as I always have.

This does not match any of my remaining symptom profiles (Hallucinations, Functional Impairment, Duration, Psychotic Symptoms Duration).

patient.answer:
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, besides what I just told you about moving the chairs and the quilt squares... I don't do things like checking the locks over and over, or needing to do my chores in an exact order. 

My days are pretty simple, really. I don't have any strict routines that I get stuck on or anything. So, no, I wouldn't say I do any of that kind of repeating.

inference.note: Added frontotemporal dementia (F02.80/G31.09) given new perseverative, stereotyped behaviors (moving chairs, repetitive folding) with lack of insight, alongside apathy/amotivation without depressed mood, guilt, or vegetative symptoms; retained organic personality change (F07.0) and atypical depression (F32.8) as broader alternatives given anhedonia without core depressive features.

doctor.intent: Assess for loss of social awareness/insight and inappropriate behavior, a core feature distinguishing frontotemporal dementia from apathy due to depression
doctor.question: Have you or others noticed you saying or doing things in public that seem socially inappropriate or insensitive—things you wouldn't have done before—like making blunt comments or not seeming to notice how others react to you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about socially inappropriate or insensitive behavior, such as making blunt comments or lacking social awareness (suggestive of frontotemporal dementia or similar conditions). The patient's symptom profile covers Disorganized Abnormal Behavior (moving chairs, folding quilt squares), but not socially inappropriate comments or lack of empathy/social tact. Therefore, none of the profile items directly match this question.

patient.answer: No, I don't think so. I haven't been making rude comments or anything like that. I mean, I mostly just keep to myself. I haven't noticed people getting upset with things I say, and no one's told me I'm being insensitive. So, no, I wouldn't say I've been doing anything like that.

inference.note: The presence of repetitive, stereotyped behaviors (moving chairs into rows, perseverative folding) with loss of insight, combined with profound apathy/avolition, anhedonia, but intact memory, sleep, appetite, and mood (no sadness/guilt/hopelessness), points away from a primary depressive disorder (F32.8) and away from a nonspecific frontal lobe syndrome without dementia features (F07.0). This constellation—behavioral disinhibition/perseveration plus apathy—is classic for behavioral-variant frontotemporal degeneration, supporting G31.09 and F02.80 as the leading diagnoses.

doctor.intent: Assess for executive dysfunction or difficulty managing complex daily tasks (e.g., finances, planning), which would support a dementia diagnosis versus an isolated apathy/behavioral syndrome without broader cognitive decline
doctor.question: Have you or your family noticed any trouble managing things like your finances, medications, or planning tasks that you used to handle easily on your own?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about executive dysfunction or trouble with instrumental activities of daily living (managing finances, medications, planning tasks). The patient's symptom profile does not contain a specific symptom for cognitive decline or executive dysfunction (only hallucinations, disorganized behavior, negative symptoms, functional impairment, and duration). While functional impairment mentions stepping back from choir/projects, it does not specifically address managing finances or medications.

patient.answer: No, I manage all that just fine. I still pay my own bills, and I take my pills when I'm supposed to. My daughter comes by sometimes to check in, but she hasn't had to take over my checkbook or anything. I handle my own business same as I always have.

inference.note: The finances/medication management remain intact, arguing against a general dementia process (F02.80) with functional decline. The combination of profound apathy, loss of pleasure without depressed mood, preserved memory/executive function for daily tasks, and new stereotyped/perseverative behaviors (rearranging chairs, repetitive quilt-folding) without insight is characteristic of behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia, narrowing the differential to G31.09.
